From the reflection, \(-A+B+C\equiv -1\pmod{11}\).

Also, modulo \(10\):
\[
3^{17}\equiv 3,\quad 3^{10}\equiv 9 \implies n\equiv 3+9\equiv 2\pmod{10}.
\]
So the last digit is \(B=2\).

Substitute \(B=2\):
\[
-A+2+C\equiv -1\pmod{11}
\implies C-A\equiv -3\pmod{11}.
\]
Since \(A,C\) are odd digits, \(C-A=-3\) would make \(A=C+3\) even, impossible. Thus \(C-A=8\), so \(C=A+8\). With odd digits, \(A=1,C=9\).

Therefore,
\[
100A+10B+C=100(1)+10(2)+9=129.
\]
\[
\boxed{129}
\]
